title: Policy engine: add rollout auto-rollback config schema + validation guardrails
author: Benji Okafor
release_notes: Adds schema + validation for rollout auto-mitigation (pause/rollback) on SLO breach. No behavior change unless config is present/enabled by controller.
body:
Summary
Adds a first-class schema in the policy engine for configuring SLO-driven auto-mitigation during rollouts (auto-rollback / auto-pause), including validation and safe bounds. This unblocks rollout-controller integration work by providing a typed contract for thresholds/windows, minimum sample sizes, and suppression settings.

Motivation
We’ve had multiple internal incidents/simulations where teams wanted to enable “rollback on p95/p99 latency or error-rate SLO burn” but configs were either ad-hoc or unsafe (e.g., 30s windows, no minimum volume, no debounce). This PR standardizes the config surface with explicit guardrails to reduce flapping/oscillation and ensure we can audit decisions.

What’s included
- New policy schema: RolloutAutoMitigationPolicy (wired into existing RolloutPolicy bundle)
  - action_mode: pause_only | rollback_or_pause (controller decides based on policy + rollout step type)
  - signals: latency_p95 | latency_p99 | error_rate | saturation (schema supports; controller may initially implement subset)
  - evaluation:
    - fast_burn_window: duration (default 5m)
    - slow_burn_window: duration (default 30m)
    - burn_rate_threshold_fast / burn_rate_threshold_slow
    - min_requests_fast_window / min_requests_slow_window
    - debounce: duration (holdoff after any auto action)
  - suppression:
    - suppression_window: duration (admin override / incident suppression)
    - suppress_during_incident: bool (honors incident/maintenance toggles when provided by control plane)
  - scope selectors (required): service/route, model_version, region, customer_tier

- Validation and safe bounds (server-side; rejects config at write time)
  - Duration bounds:
    - fast_burn_window: 1m–15m
    - slow_burn_window: 10m–6h
    - debounce: 2m–60m
    - suppression_window: 5m–24h
  - Window relationship: slow_burn_window must be >= 2x fast_burn_window
  - Minimum sample gating: min_requests_* must be >= 200 for hosted/self-serve tiers; >= 100 for dedicated/private tiers (config can be higher, not lower)
  - Burn-rate thresholds: must be within 1.0–50.0 (prevents “always breach” or impossible values)
  - Allowed combinations:
    - If action_mode=rollback_or_pause, debounce must be >= 5m (prevents repeated rollbacks)
    - If signals include saturation, slow_burn_window must be >= 30m (reduces false positives due to transient batching shifts)
  - Guardrail defaults applied when fields omitted (explicitly versioned): default_policy_version=1

- Documentation + examples
Adds an internal doc snippet + JSON example used by Console policy editor.

Example config (as stored in policy bundle)
{
  "rolloutAutoMitigation": {
    "enabled": true,
    "actionMode": "ROLLBACK_OR_PAUSE",
    "signals": ["LATENCY_P99", "ERROR_RATE"],
    "evaluation": {
      "fastBurnWindow": "5m",
      "slowBurnWindow": "30m",
      "burnRateThresholdFast": 10.0,
      "burnRateThresholdSlow": 2.0,
      "minRequestsFastWindow": 300,
      "minRequestsSlowWindow": 1200,
      "debounce": "10m"
    },
    "suppression": {
      "suppressionWindow": "30m",
      "suppressDuringIncident": true
    }
  }
}

Backwards compatibility
- Existing rollout policies remain valid; rolloutAutoMitigation is optional and defaults to disabled.
- No controller behavior is changed by this PR alone; controller will read this config behind its own feature flag.

Testing
- Unit tests for validation boundaries and defaulting.
- Golden config tests for JSON (Console) <-> internal policy model round-tripping.

Operational notes
- Validation errors are surfaced as structured policy errors (code=INVALID_ARGUMENT) with field paths so Console can show inline warnings.
- Added metric: policy_validation_error_total{policy_type="rollout_auto_mitigation",field=...} (low cardinality; field is enum-mapped).

Follow-ups
- Controller integration will implement burn-rate evaluation semantics (ENG-4821/ENG-4861) and will consume this schema.
- RBAC: wiring admin-only suppression writes (INT-8832) is in progress; this PR only adds the fields and validation, not permission changes.

Screenshots
N/A (schema-only change).
commits: policy-engine: add RolloutAutoMitigationPolicy to rollout policy bundle
policy-engine: validation + safe bounds for durations, thresholds, min sample sizes
policy-engine: defaulting + versioning for rolloutAutoMitigation config
policy-engine: golden tests for JSON round-trip and error field paths
docs: add internal example snippet for Console policy editor
review_summary: Jordan requested tightening the window relationship constraint and adding explicit error field paths for Console. Sean asked for tier-specific minimum request floors and a hard cap on suppression duration to avoid “infinite suppression.” Kevin requested ensuring suppression justification is not part of this schema (to avoid storing free-form text in policy bundles) and that audit logging covers who/why elsewhere. All addressed; approved by Jordan/Sean/Ethan; Allison acked metric labeling changes.
conversation_excerpt: Jordan Lee (review): Can we enforce slow_window >= 2x fast_window? Otherwise teams will set 5m/6m and we’ll flap.
Benji Okafor (author): Added constraint slow >= 2x fast + unit tests; updated error path to rolloutAutoMitigation.evaluation.slowBurnWindow.
Sean Gallagher (review): Please add tier-aware min request floors. Hosted gets noisy under low volume and will trigger false positives.
Benji Okafor (author): Added per-tier floors (self-serve/hosted >= 200, dedicated/private >= 100) with validation and docs note.
Kevin Osei (review): Avoid any free-form justification in policy (privacy/compliance). Make sure audit log captures justification separately.
Benji Okafor (author): Confirmed: schema contains only enums/durations/numbers. Justification stays in audit events (tracked in ENG-4864).
Ethan Park (approval): Looks good. Error paths and defaulting will help Console. Ship it.
